screening_decisions.reason: This is an observational study analyzing complications in 5,851 consecutively induced abortions. It does not compare different surgical methods and is not a randomized controlled trial.

Randomized controlled trial comparing conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) vs manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for first trimester abortion (gestational age <56 days). 200 women randomized to either surgical method.

This is a historical epidemiological analysis using national statistics data to compare mortality/morbidity trends before and after Roe v Wade. Not a randomized trial and does not compare surgical methods.

This RCT compares prostaglandin suppository vs placebo for cervical preparation BEFORE vacuum aspiration. All women received the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration). The intervention being tested is preoperative medication, not different surgical methods.
Randomized controlled trial comparing dilatation and curettage (D&C) vs vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. 420 women randomly assigned to either surgical method.
Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration vs electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion (<10 weeks). 84 women randomized to either surgical method.
Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) vs electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) for first trimester abortion. 127 women randomly assigned to either surgical method.

While this study compares vacuum aspiration vs dilatation and curettage, the abstract does not state that randomization was used. It describes 47 women undergoing abortion with 23 by vacuum aspiration and 24 by D&C, but does not explicitly mention randomization. Without clear evidence of RCT design, this study is excluded.

This RCT compares metal vs flexible plastic cannulae for performing vacuum aspiration. Both groups received the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration); the comparison is between equipment types within the same technique, not between different surgical methods.
Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspirator vs electric vacuum curettage for first trimester abortion. 114 women randomized to either surgical method.
